---
title: "Optional R: repeat one familiar analysis"
---

This walkthrough repeats the [animal oxygen-consumption practical](../practicals/animal-measurements.qmd).
**It is optional and adds no core physiology outcome.** Complete the biological
question, independent-unit discussion and one worked calculation first. The
teacher may use this supplied code within the existing analysis time or leave
it out entirely.

## What you need

Use the downloaded student project with `physiology.Rproj`, `data/` and
`optional-computing/` kept in their supplied relative positions. R and RStudio
with the Intro Computing packages `readr`, `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `knitr` and
`rmarkdown` are needed to run and render. Set up packages before the session
using the supported Intro Computing instructions; do not put installation
commands in an analysis report. HTML rendering also needs Pandoc, supplied
by RStudio or Quarto in the teaching environment.

The source files are [analysis.R](analysis.R) and
[respirometry.Rmd](respirometry.Rmd). The input is
[animal-respirometry.csv](../data/animal-respirometry.csv), documented in the
[data dictionary](../data/README.md). These values are simulated.

## Read before running

The function in `analysis.R` imports and checks the table, calculates a
background-corrected amount, divides by time and mass, summarises groups and
plots each animal. Its checks suit this deliberately complete teaching
dataset; a real dataset needs protocol-specific checks and explicit handling
of missing or unexpected readings.

The calculation is the same one already used by hand:

```r
oxygen_used_umol <- (initial - final - blank) * water_volume_l
rate_umol_min_g <- oxygen_used_umol / duration_min / mass_g
```

Each row is one animal, so grouped counts are animal counts here. That would
not automatically be true for repeated measurements from one animal.

## Run from the project root

Open `physiology.Rproj` and create a source script or use the supplied script
as a reference. In the R console, starting at the project root, run:

```r
source("optional-computing/analysis.R")
analysis <- analyse_respirometry("data/animal-respirometry.csv")
analysis$rates
analysis$summary
analysis$plot
```

Locate A01 and A02 in the output. Their rates should be 0.18 and 0.20 µmol
O₂ min⁻¹ g⁻¹. Group means should be 0.20 and 0.325. Explain why the mean
is higher in the warmer simulated group, and why this alone does not show
better growth or performance.

## Render the supplied report

Open `optional-computing/respirometry.Rmd` and use **Knit**. R Markdown
evaluates relative input paths from that document's folder, so the report
uses `../data/animal-respirometry.csv` and sources `analysis.R` beside it.
The project-root commands above instead use `data/...`. These are two
descriptions of the same file from different working directories.

The complete report produces a self-contained HTML file next to the `.Rmd`.
Read its design, calculation and limitations, not only its figure. Restart R
and Knit again without creating console objects first. Keep the source,
function, dictionary and input with the HTML if sharing the work.

## A small adaptation task

Copy the report before changing it. Add one sentence explaining the independent
unit and one identifying an assumption you would need to check in a real
experiment. In the plotting function, improve one axis label without changing
the physiological quantity or units. Re-render and confirm the numerical
results are unchanged. No new statistics or data reshaping is required.

If paths or rendering take over the practical, return to the worked table and
hand-drawn plot. The aim is physiological interpretation. Teachers can supply
the complete figure and result rather than requiring independent code writing.
